title: Proper/open comparison for pro-etale module sheaves
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $p:V\to T$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves of rings $A_H$ on the small pro-etale sites of $H=U,V,W,T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $p_*,r_*$ and $i^*,k^*$ for direct image and exact inverse image with constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $i_!,k_!$ for extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero].
For a module sheaf $M$ on $U$, let
$$\lambda_M:i^*p_*k_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}r_*k^*k_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}r_*M$$
be open restriction followed by the inverse of the open unit. Open restriction is the identification given, on a pro-etale $Q\to W$, by evaluating both sides on $V\times_TQ=U\times_WQ$. Let
$$\gamma_M=\varepsilon_{i,p_*k_!M}\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}):i_!r_*M\longrightarrow p_*k_!M$$
be its transpose under $i_!\dashv i^*$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Then $\gamma_M$ is an isomorphism, natural in $M$. There is no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $i$, no boundedness condition, and no etale-origin condition on $M$.

source.place: Steps 3–4: proper/open comparison before taking the exceptional-adjoint mate, degree-zero support input; agent-extracted pro-etale sheaf obligation, not a theorem asserted by the etale source. Etale analogue: literature/stacks-project/more-etale.tex, Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, case (b). Pro-etale open functors: proetale.tex, Tag 09AE, label definition-extension-zero; Tag 09BN, label lemma-open-immersion.

proof.text: First record the sectionwise meaning of the map, including its normalization. For an open immersion $j$, restriction of the defining zero-or-one-summand presheaf to objects over the open is the original sheaf. The localization equivalence identifies its coverings with the intrinsic site's coverings, so its sheafification restricted there is the original sheaf as well. Thus the open unit $M\to j^*j_!M$ is an isomorphism. Direct image is evaluation on the fibre product, so $i^*p_*k_!M=r_*k^*k_!M$ by the equality of fibre products in the statement, with the same restriction and scalar maps. These identifications give precisely $\lambda_M$. Under the stated adjunction, $\gamma_M$ is the unique map whose open restriction, followed by $\lambda_M$, is the identity on $r_*M$; the triangle identity gives this directly from $\gamma_M=\varepsilon_i i_!(\lambda_M^{-1})$.

source.place: Tags 09AE (definition-extension-zero), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion); sectionwise verification of the chosen transpose

proof.text: For any module sheaf $N$, the counit $j_!j^*N\to N$ is induced by the presheaf map which is the identity $N(B)\to N(B)$ when $B$ factors through the open, and is $0\to N(B)$ otherwise. This map is sectionwise injective. Exact module sheafification makes the counit a monomorphism. Consequently $\gamma_M$ is a monomorphism, since $i_!(\lambda_M^{-1})$ is invertible. The same argument shows that, for opens $O_0\subset O\subset H$ and a sheaf $F$ on $O$, the canonical map $(O_0\hookrightarrow H)_!(F|_{O_0})\to(O\hookrightarrow H)_!F$ is monic: the map of defining presheaves is the identity on objects over $O_0$ and the inclusion of zero on all other objects. We will use these inclusions to glue local lifts.

source.place: Tag 09AE and the zero-extension presheaf; module-sheafification exactness is sites-modules.tex Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact

proof.text: It suffices to prove surjectivity on every affine object $Q\to T$ of the small pro-etale site: every site object has an affine Zariski covering, which is a pro-etale covering, and sections and their equalities glue. Localize the square at $Q$, writing $V_Q=V\times_TQ$, $W_Q=W\times_TQ$, and $U_Q=V_Q\times_QW_Q$; restrict $M$ to $U_Q$. All coefficient identifications are those of localization of the same constant ring. The extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism identifies restrictions of $i_!$ and $k_!$ with extension by zero for these opens; direct image restricts by its fibre-product evaluation formula. These identifications preserve $\gamma$, because its restriction to $W_Q$ is the inverse of the same $\lambda$, and the open adjunction makes that restriction determine the map. Properness of $p_Q$ and openness of $k_Q$ follow by base change. We may therefore work over an affine base $Q=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and prove the assertion there. Properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness of $V_Q\to Q$.

source.place: Tags 09AE, 09BN; localization and fibre-product evaluations, not proper base change for arbitrary sheaves

proof.text: First suppose that $W_Q\subset Q$ is quasi-compact. The principal opens form a basis directly from the Zariski topology: the complement of $V(J)$ is $\bigcup_{f\in J}D(f)$. Quasi-compactness therefore gives a finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ with $W_Q=\bigcup_aD(f_a)$, allowing the empty list. Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, $S=\{s\in R:s\bmod I\text{ is a unit}\}$, and $Q^\sim=\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$. The closed-localization covering theorem supplies the pro-etale cover $\{D(f_a)\to Q,Q^\sim\to Q\}$. Every point of $Q^\sim$ specializes within $Q^\sim$ to $Z^\sim=Z\times_QQ^\sim$ by the arbitrary-ideal specialization-localization theorem. On every $D(f_a)$ the map $\gamma$ is already the identity through $\lambda$, by Step 1. It remains to show that both sheaves have zero sections over $Q^\sim$.

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), finite localization cover in the proof; Tag 096V (lemma-localization), f=1

proof.text: The source $(i_!r_*M)(Q^\sim)$ is zero. Indeed base change for extension by zero identifies its restriction with extension by zero from $W_Q\times_QQ^\sim$. The closed-immersion base-change theorem makes $Z^\sim\hookrightarrow Q^\sim$ a closed immersion. That open is disjoint from $Z^\sim$, and $Q^\sim$ is affine with every point specializing into $Z^\sim$. Apply the specialization-zero theorem. Although that theorem is stated for abelian sheaves, it applies to the underlying abelian sheaf of this module extension: the module-sheafification definition says its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of the same zero-extension presheaf. A module whose underlying abelian group is zero is zero.

source.place: Tag 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero), applied to the affine specialization localization

proof.text: Write $P=V_Q\times_QQ^\sim$ and $C=P\times_{Q^\sim}Z^\sim$. The map $h:P\to Q^\sim$ is proper, and $C\hookrightarrow P$ is a closed immersion by closed-immersion base change. For each $x\in P$, choose a specialization $z$ of $h(x)$ in $Z^\sim$. Since $h$ is closed, $h(\overline{\{x\}})$ is closed and contains $h(x)$; hence it contains $z$. Choose $x_z\in\overline{\{x\}}$ over $z$. Thus every $x$ specializes to a point of $C$. This argument uses the closed-map part of the definition of properness, after base change, and proves the required specialization lifting without any claim about geometric-stalk conservativity. The scheme $P$ is quasi-compact because it is proper over the affine scheme $Q^\sim$. It is also separated over the affine base $Q^\sim$, by the definition of properness.

source.place: Tag 01W1 (definition-proper), universally closed condition, combined with Tag 096V

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $P=\bigcup_b B_b$. For the ideal $J_b$ defining $C\cap B_b$ in $B_b=\operatorname{Spec}R_b$, form $L_b=\operatorname{Spec}(S_b^{-1}R_b)$ with $S_b$ the elements invertible modulo $J_b$. The specialization-localization theorem makes $L_b\to B_b$ weakly etale and identifies its image with the points specializing inside $B_b$ to $C\cap B_b$. Every point $x\in P$ lies in the image of some $L_b$: its specialization $x_z\in C$ from Step 6 lies in some $B_b$; an open containing $x_z$ also contains its generalization $x$, so this specialization occurs inside $B_b$. The finite family $L_b\to P$ is a pro-etale covering. To check its covering condition on an affine open $B\subset P$, note that $B\cap B_b$ is affine, hence quasi-compact, by the affine-open intersection theorem for a separated scheme over an affine base, and its inverse image in $L_b$ is quasi-compact: cover $B\cap B_b$ by finitely many principal opens of $B_b$; their localization inverse images are principal affine opens of $L_b$. Finitely many such affine opens, as $b$ varies, cover $B$ by joint surjectivity. This is exactly the fpqc covering condition in the pro-etale-site definition.

source.place: Tag 096V (lemma-localization), applied on finitely many affine charts; covering condition of the small pro-etale site

proof.text: On each $L_b$, every point specializes into $C\times_PL_b$. The open $U_Q\times_{V_Q}P$ is disjoint from $C$, so the specialization-zero theorem applied to the affine site object $L_b\to P$ says that its extension-by-zero sheaf has zero sections on $L_b$. The underlying abelian sheaf of the module extension is the abelian sheafification of its zero-extension presheaf, so the vanishing applies to its underlying groups and hence to its modules. Base change for extension by zero identifies this sheaf with the restriction of $k_!M$ to $P$. Separatedness of a sheaf on the covering from Step 7 therefore gives $(k_!M)(P)=0$. By direct-image evaluation this is $(p_*k_!M)(Q^\sim)=0$. Consequently, a section of $p_*k_!M$ over $Q$ lifts over every member of the covering in Step 4: uniquely over each $D(f_a)$ by Step 1, and by zero over $Q^\sim$. Monicity from Step 2 makes these lifts agree on every overlap, so they glue to a preimage over $Q$. This proves bijectivity of $\gamma(Q)$. The affine base $Q$ in this argument was arbitrary. For any affine site object $B\to Q$, Step 3 identifies the restricted comparison with the comparison for $V_Q\times_Q B\to B$. This morphism is proper, and the inverse image of $W_Q=\bigcup_aD(f_a)$ is the finite union of the corresponding principal opens of $B$. Thus the just-proved assertion about sections over an arbitrary affine base applies to this base-changed square and gives bijectivity of $\gamma(B)$. Bijectivity on these affine objects and the sheaf condition prove the quasi-compact-open case. We do not assert that the restrictions to $Q^\sim$ are zero sheaves: only their sections on its identity object vanish.

source.place: Tag 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero), followed by separatedness on the explicit specialization cover

proof.text: Now allow $W_Q$ to be an arbitrary open. Take $s\in(k_!M)(V_Q)=(p_*k_!M)(Q)$. This section has local representatives in the defining extension presheaf. More explicitly, module sheafification is abelian sheafification; its unit becomes an isomorphism after sheafification by the reflector's universal property. Applying the sheafification/local-bijection theorem to that unit makes it locally surjective. Thus there is a pro-etale covering on which $s$ is represented by presheaf sections. Since $V_Q$ is quasi-compact, first choose a finite affine open cover and then use the fpqc covering condition over each of these affines to refine to a finite family of affine objects $H_c\to V_Q$ carrying representatives. A representative is zero unless $H_c\to V_Q$ factors through $U_Q$. For each of the finitely many objects carrying a nonzero representative (which therefore do factor through $U_Q$), the image of the affine $H_c$ in $Q$ is quasi-compact and contained in $W_Q$. Cover those images by finitely many principal opens of $Q$ contained in $W_Q$, and let $W_0$ be their union. Then $W_0\subset W_Q$ is a quasi-compact open and every $H_c$ carrying a nonzero representative factors through $U_0=V_Q\times_QW_0$: image containment gives a unique map $H_c\to W_0$ by the open-factorization theorem, and then the fibre-product universal property gives the map to $U_0$. The map $H_c\to U_0$ is a site object by weakly etale localization. The empty union is allowed when all representatives are zero.

source.place: Tag 00WK (sites-lemma-sections-sheafification), via the existing local-bijection criterion; Tag 09AE and finite affine refinement of fpqc coverings

proof.text: Put $M_0=M|_{U_0}$ and let $k_0:U_0\hookrightarrow V_Q$. The canonical map $k_{0!}M_0\to k_!M$ is monic by Step 2. Every local representative of $s$ constructed in Step 9 lifts to $k_{0!}M_0$: use the same section of $M$ on an $H_c$ factoring through $U_0$, and zero on all other $H_c$. Their lifts agree on overlaps because their images agree with $s$ and the map is monic. The sheaf condition glues them to a section $s_0\in(k_{0!}M_0)(V_Q)$ mapping to $s$. This establishes the needed quasi-compact support reduction directly on sections, with no assertion that proper pro-etale direct image preserves arbitrary colimits.

source.place: Tags 09AE and 00WK; monomorphism and gluing of the finite local lifts from Step 9

proof.text: Apply the quasi-compact-open case (Steps 4--8) to $W_0\hookrightarrow Q$ and the same proper map $V_Q\to Q$. Its isomorphism $\gamma_0$ gives a section $t_0\in(i_{0!}r_{0*}M_0)(Q)$ mapping to $s_0$. There is a canonical map $a:i_{0!}r_{0*}M_0\to i_!r_*M$: restriction of $r_*M$ to $W_0$ is $r_{0*}M_0$ by fibre-product evaluation, and on zero-extension presheaves $a$ is the identity on objects over $W_0$ and zero elsewhere. Let $b:p_*k_{0!}M_0\to p_*k_!M$ be the inclusion-induced map. Then $\gamma\circ a=b\circ\gamma_0$: both maps have source $i_{0!}r_{0*}M_0$, and under the open adjunction for $i_0$ their transposes agree, since on $W_0$ all the open-unit identifications and the inclusions in question are the identity on $r_{0*}M_0$. It follows that $a(t_0)$ maps to $s$. Hence $\gamma$ is surjective on sections of every affine site object, as well as injective by Step 2, and is therefore an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Tags 09AE and 09BN; explicit open-adjunction compatibility for the finite-support reduction

proof.text: Finally all identifications in $\lambda_M$ are natural in $M$: fibre-product evaluation commutes with a morphism of sheaves, and the open unit is a natural transformation. Thus for $u:M\to N$, $\lambda_N\circ i^*p_*k_!(u)=r_*(u)\circ\lambda_M$. Taking inverses and using naturality of the counit in the defining formula gives $p_*k_!(u)\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ i_!r_*(u)$. The componentwise inverses satisfy the inverse naturality square by cancellation. This proves naturality of the isomorphism for the exact map specified in the statement. No step imposed boundedness, etale origin, or quasi-compactness of the original open immersion.

source.place: Tag 09AE, adjunction naturality; normalization required before the exceptional-adjoint mate
